To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the variance partitioning showed similar results for the four arthropod datasets and that ground beetle data provided more detailed information on vegetation characteristics and soil contamination levels.

(1) ground beetles can provide a good indication of the relative impact of different environmental characteristics on terrestrial arthopod diversity, (2) the higher degree of taxon-specificity in ground beetles can help to identify the most sensitive arthropod groups and (3) the higher taxonomic resolution in ground beetles will be beneficial for identifying the most sensitive arthopod species.

(1) the relative contribution of different environmental variables for explaining variation in arthropod assembles was similar for the four arthropod datasets and (2) a higher degree of arthropod taxonomic detail was beneficial for investigating the effects of environmental variables in terms of taxonomical diversity and community composition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of relatively coarse arthropod data for environmental monitoring and assessment, which is important in view of the increasing need for monitoring programmes with reduced sampling efforts.
the question of whether a relatively coarse arthropod taxonomic level can be used to assess environmental characteristics in floodplain areas.
the use of arthropod datasets with different taxonomic detail for assessing the influence of environmental characteristics on arthropod community structure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of ground beetle data is most valuable for studying effects of environmental pollution, but that the other three datasets provide valuable additional information on the influence of environmental factors on arthropod communities in general.
the use of different taxonomic levels is a valuable addition to ecological research.
all arthropod datasets are useful in their own right and that the most suitable dataset for answering specific research questions depends on the research objective.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the choice of taxonomic detail depends on the research question and that the use of coarse data is not necessarily less valuable.
coarse taxonomic data are sufficient to identify important environmental characteristics for structuring arthonopod assemblages in a floodplain area.
the ground beetle dataset provided a more detailed and specific picture of the relations between the arthropod assembalges and the environment than the other datasets.
The main takeaway from our work is that
coarse taxonomic data is a useful and cost-effective tool for monitoring environmental change in lowland floodplain ecosystems.

relatively coarse taxonomic datasets are already able to provide a valuable indication for the relative importance of the different environmental factors that shape terrestrial arthropod communities in heterogeneous landscapes.
the taxonomic resolution of the dataset used to study the effects of environmental characteristics on arthropod assembles should be tailored to the research question at hand.
